key_insight: SFRBE--RaNN adaptively reallocates random neural network features and enriches the trial space to better match PDE structure, scale, and nonlinearity while keeping the solve least-squares based.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a practical way to improve accuracy for localized, multiscale, and nonlinear PDEs without abandoning the efficiency of randomized neural solvers.
method: SFR redistributes a fixed feature budget by regional residual indicators and optimizes local weight scales.
RBE adds only nonredundant features by screening activation families, removing already-represented directions, and choosing the smallest valid prefix.
For nonlinear operators, candidates are first screened with a frozen operator and then verified by the full nonlinear residual.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical experiments on localized, multiscale, and nonlinear space-time PDEs, alongside theoretical residual identities and error/probability bounds for linear problems.
watch_item: The adaptive pipeline adds screening, residual checks, and optimization steps, so implementation complexity and compute overhead may increase relative to plain randomized features.
paper_title: Adaptive Randomized Neural Networks for PDEs: Structure-Aware Feature Redistribution and Residual-Driven Block Enrichment
